result.note: Weekly wrap with several institutional actions; tested the Cabinet, court and GST Council actions, the RBI's rate hike, and the opposition march on the Election Commission.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs of institutions and the actions attributed to them in India in the week ending 10 October 2026:
items: Union Cabinet — INR 100 billion of support for mid-sized manufacturers
A court — forced the food regulator to ease its energy-drink crackdown
GST Council — recommended stripping tax officers of their arrest powers
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: All three pairs match the story. The Cabinet backed mid-sized manufacturers with INR 100 billion, a court made the food regulator ease its energy-drink crackdown, and the GST Council also recommended automating refunds. TBB framed these as India loosening its grip on business.
questions.source: The Cabinet put INR 100 billion behind mid-sized manufacturers, a court forced the food regulator to ease its rushed energy-drink crackdown on Wednesday, and the GST Council recommended stripping tax officers of their arrest powers and automating refunds on Friday.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Reserve Bank of India's policy action on 8 October 2026:
items: It was the Reserve Bank's first rate hike in nearly four years.
It marked a shift towards monetary easing.
Imported oil and a weak monsoon were among the pressures behind the move.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the story describes the hike as a shift to calibrated tightening, not easing. The Reserve Bank raised rates for the first time in nearly four years amid concerns over imported oil and a weak monsoon.
questions.source: on Thursday the Reserve Bank delivered its first rate hike in nearly four years, a shift to calibrated tightening as imported oil and a weak monsoon cause it to worry about growth.

questions.prompt: On 7 October 2026, police detained opposition MPs marching in New Delhi. Consider the following statements:
items: Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi was among those detained.
The MPs were marching on the Election Commission to demand that its chief resign.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both statements are correct. The MPs, including Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, were detained while marching on the Election Commission to demand its chief resign. TBB cited the episode as the government tightening its grip on politics.
questions.source: Police detained opposition MPs, Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi among them, as they marched on the Election Commission on Wednesday to demand its chief resign
